(2026) used one LAMOST MRS-N plate to suggest that the Silk Nebula, a $17^\circ$-long \Oiii~$λ$5007 filament in Gemini, is possibly associated with a supernova remnant at a fiducial distance of $\sim$160\,pc. We test this against their published values and independent archival data. The \Ni\ airglow in their blue-arm spectrum lies at air, topocentric rest wavelengths, so their \Oiii\ velocities omit the heliocentric correction and are $10.1\pm1.0$\,\kms\ too high. Corrected and combined with DESI DR1 and SDSS spectra, \Oiii\ lies at \vhel\ $=+13.3\pm1.0$\,\kms, the velocity of \Nii\ and of the local warm ionized medium (WIM). Their \Ha\ velocities are 4.5--6.7\,\kms\ redder than \Nii. Their tabulated distances are in kpc, not units of 100\,pc, and kinematic distances carry no information in this direction. Their surface brightness exceeds independent measurements (1.4--2.5 rayleighs) by factors of 4.6--8.6. Their red-line shock criteria are met equally in their nebula-free background region and describe the WIM; their other remnant diagnostics do not constrain the filament. DESI and SDSS spectra show that the filament is Balmer-dark (\Oiii/\Hb\ $>11$) and \Oii-strong, with \ion{He}{2}/\Oiii\ $<0.026$; GALEX shows a coincident ultraviolet ridge, with no \Ha, \ion{H}{1}, dust or X-ray counterpart. These properties, and the lack of an ionizing source, exclude photoionization equilibrium and complete radiative shocks and match a column-truncated radiative shock of $\sim$80--120\,\kms\ seen edge-on, plausibly on the limb of the Monogem Ring at $\sim$250--320\,pc. Far-ultraviolet and deep optical spectroscopy, a two-epoch proper motion and high-ion absorption toward bracketing white dwarfs would be decisive.

title: Willmore stability of minimal surfaces in the n-sphere
authors: Rob Kusner, Peng Wang
abstract: We prove that the Lawson minimal surface $ξ_{g,1}$ in $S^3$ is strongly stable for the Willmore bending energy $W$ and remains strongly $W$-stable in $S^n$ for every $n \geq4$; our proof starts with a new lower bound on the area-index of $ξ_{m,k}$ for $m\geq k>1$. Next we observe that each of the $ξ_{m,k}$ and the Karcher-Pinkall-Sterling minimal surfaces in $S^3$, as well as the equilateral minimal torus in $S^5$, is the unique $W$-minimizer in its conformal class, up to Möbius transformations of $S^n$. Finally, we show that although the equilateral minimal torus is $W$-stable in $S^n$ for every $n \geq5$, it is neither strongly $W$-stable nor a local $W$-minimizer: it has a 2-dimensional space of $W$-Jacobi fields on which almost everywhere the third-variation of $W$ is nonzero.

title: Triplet adiabatic potential energy surfaces for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X$^1Σ_g^+$, a$^3Π_u$) reaction and quasiclassical trajectory dynamics
authors: A. Veselinova-Marinova, S. Gómez-Carrasco, L. González-Sánchez, A. Zanchet, P. G. Jambrina, C. Sanz-Sanz
abstract: We present three global adiabatic potential energy surfaces (PESs) for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$, a $^3Π_u$) to CO(X$^1Σ^+$) + C($^3$P) reaction, computed at the icMRCI+Q/aug-cc-pVTZ level. This reaction is relevant to combustion chemistry, atmospheric processes, and astrochemistry. Since the energy difference between the $^1Σ_g^+$ and $^3Π_u$ states of C$_2$ is smaller than the zero-point energy, both states mix upon interaction with the approaching O atom. Consequently, the PESs exhibit a double-well topography in the reactant valley. Beyond this feature, the three PESs display markedly different topographies. The 1 $^3A''$ PES features a deep minimum 7.16 eV below the O + C$_2$ entrance channel. In contrast, the 2 $^3A''$ and 1 $^3A'$ surfaces possess shallower collinear wells ($\approx$ 5.7 eV) and strong angular anisotropy arising from avoided crossings with higher-lying triplet states. The analytical fits reproduce the \textit{ab initio} data with root-mean-square (RMS) deviations of 0.022--0.028 eV over an energy interval exceeding 13 eV. Quasiclassical trajectory (QCT) calculations reveal higher reactivity on the barrierless $1\,^3A''$ surface compared to the $2\,^3A''$ PES, where an angle-dependent entrance barrier reduces the cross sections. Furthermore, cross sections for reactions initiated from C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$) and C$_2$(a $^3Π_u$) are remarkably similar for the three PESs, regardless of the initial rovibrational state.

title: Federated Learning for Unmanned Aerial Systems: A Screened Bibliometric Census of an Emergent Sub-Literature
authors: Ameen Ur Rehman, Ali Nasir
abstract: We census the literature at the intersection of federated learning (FL) and unmanned aerial systems (UAS) with a broad Scopus query that combines FL, UAV, and delivery/logistics terms (Computer Science and Engineering, 2022--2026). The export holds \textbf{14,965 records}, but only \textbf{7.9\%} of the 14,945 unique records mention both an FL term and a UAV term in title, abstract, or author keywords. That screen leaves \textbf{1,185 records}: 90 in 2022, 361 in 2025, and 332 already indexed for 2026. The screened share of each year's raw output stays near 7.5\%, so the growth is not an artefact of the screen. Term-definition, document-type, and complete-year checks leave the leading venue (\emph{IEEE Internet of Things Journal}, 111 papers, $h{=}30$) and the leading country (China, 628 affiliation instances) unchanged. A manual read of 30 records finds 14 of 26 full papers (54\%, 95\% CI 35--71\%) substantively about FL for UAVs, so the corpus counts keyword co-occurrence, not only focused work. Counting authors by Scopus ID gives 4,095 authors with Lotka exponent $n{=}3.15$ ($R^2{=}0.996$); name strings would merge distinct people and understate the author count by 31\%. An OpenAlex export under the same screen yields 147 records, 74\% of them in the Scopus corpus, but the two exports are not matched populations, so we do not read the volume gap as coverage alone. Finally, of 228 records with a delivery-adjacent term, only 5 (2.2\%) mention \emph{parcel}, \emph{last-mile}, or \emph{courier} (14, or 6.1\%, if \emph{package} counts); the rest reflect transportation, traffic, and generic-logistics idiom. Keyword screening alone therefore cannot isolate last-mile drone-delivery research from the surrounding UAV-networking literature.

title: Sourcing vector perturbations in warm inflation through shear viscous effects
authors: Arjun Berera, Suddhasattwa Brahma, Zizang Qiu, Rudnei O. Ramos
abstract: Vector modes are generally believed not to play a significant role in standard cosmological perturbation theory because they decay rapidly. Non-equilibrium dynamics in the radiation bath present during warm inflation can lead to shear viscous effects, requiring a description beyond the perfect-fluid approximation. We adopt the fluctuating hydrodynamic approach to account for stochastic anisotropic stress related to shear viscosity. We show that the vector mode obeys a constrained Langevin equation in an inflationary background. The resulting power spectrum, considered in the weak-viscosity regime, is proportional to the shear viscosity and it also depends on the Hubble slow-roll parameter $ε$, decaying approximately as $a^{-(1-ε)}$. This behaviour is significantly slower than the unsourced, non-viscous power spectrum, which decays as $a^{-4}$. The continuously sourced vector modes, nevertheless, decay on superhorizon scales, and the illustrative benchmark parameter choices adopted in our numerical examples give a negligible late-time vector-to-scalar ratio. Despite the absence of direct large-scale observable vector signatures, the main results establish a source of vector perturbations during warm inflation and provide a framework for studying possible secondary effects along with large-scale white noises in the vector channel.

title: Improving the signal-to-noise ratio through postselection of coincident detections in anticounterfeiting and quantum key distribution
authors: Paula Wieteska-Bajak, Mohamed Hatifi, Renaud Mathevet, Vincent Lacombe, Jerome Wenger, Thomas Durt
abstract: In quantum communications and other photon-counting applications, reliably detecting weak optical signals against a strong noise background remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, we develop a simple idea: when a signal is carried by pairs (or more generally multiplets) of photons emitted simultaneously, postselection of coincident detections recorded on two detectors makes it possible to improve-sometimes drastically-the Signal to Noise Ratio. Essentially, this is made possible by the fact that genuine and accidental coincidences scale differently with the width of the postselection window. As long as the window remains wide enough to retain detections from the same pair, the genuine coincidence rate is approximately unchanged. In contrast, coincidences formed from independent clicks decrease linearly as the window is narrowed. The resulting signal-to-noise ratio, therefore, increases inversely with the window width. Our approach makes it possible to reveal photon-pair signals that are otherwise hidden beneath a much stronger uncorrelated background. We analyze here applications of this idea to quantum key distribution, metrology, and anti-counterfeiting.

title: Uninorm constructions on bounded trellises via closure and interior operators
authors: Zhenyu Xiu
abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which six closure- or interior-based operations on bounded trellises are uninorms. These operations incorporate triangular norms, triangular conorms, or both, and form three order-dual pairs. Since the underlying pseudo-order need not be transitive and meet and join need not be associative, standard lattice arguments do not apply directly. Under a fixed ambient transitivity assumption, the first pair is characterized by image, monotonicity, and compatibility conditions for the associated maps on elements incomparable with the neutral element; an additional comparison condition used in earlier sufficient constructions is shown to be redundant. Complete characterizations are also obtained for the variants with an absorbing endpoint, including both nondegenerate and degenerate interval cases. For the pair involving both a triangular norm and a triangular conorm, we derive exact comparison conditions requiring the triangular norm to take the value~$0$, or dually the triangular conorm to take the value~$1$, in the relevant cases. These conditions reduce to the usual incomparability assumptions in the absence of nontrivial zero- or one-divisors. On bounded lattices, the closure and interior conditions simplify to explicit identities or image restrictions. Finite proper-trellis examples clarify the role and limitations of the ambient transitivity assumptions.

title: Learn, Freeze, and Transfer an Activation Function Across Architectures
authors: Arun Prakash A
abstract: Transfer learning typically reuses knowledge acquired by a source network through its learned weights. We investigate whether a learned activation function can also be transferred and remain useful in networks trained from scratch. We study this complementary form of transfer through a learn-freeze-transfer protocol, in which the activation is optimized jointly with a source network in a single training run, and is then frozen and reused in target networks trained from scratch. A pointwise activation with globally shared parameters is independent of layer dimensions and can therefore be incorporated into networks of different architectures trained from scratch. We instantiate this protocol with FAct, a five-parameter activation represented by a two-harmonic truncated Fourier series, initialized from a Fourier approximation of GELU and learned in a Vision Transformer (ViT) on ImageNet-1K. When reused in a ViT of the same architecture trained from scratch on ImageNet-1K, the frozen activation (Frozen FAct) improves top-1 accuracy by 1.46 percentage points over GELU. Across four smaller target architectures (standard ViT, Swin Transformer, linear-attention ViT, and MLP-Mixer) and four image-classification datasets, it achieves the highest mean accuracy among eleven activation functions in 15 of 16 settings under a common training configuration, with improvements of up to 1.71 percentage points over the best conventional activation. When the learning rate and weight decay are tuned separately for each activation under the same search budget, Frozen FAct still ranks first in 11 of the 16 settings, second in four, and fourth in one. These results provide empirical evidence that a learned activation function can retain its usefulness when transferred across vision architectures, independently of the weights with which it was learned.

title: A Three-Factor Hull-White Scenario Generator for Macro-Financial Stress Forecasting
authors: Ahmad Qadi, Thomas Schröder, Francesca Medda
abstract: This paper builds a scenario engine that maps a yield-curve path into a distribution of macro-financial outcomes. A three-factor Hull-White model generates arbitrage-free curves whose factors are simulated under the physical measure, with an estimated and reported market price of risk. A Minnesota-prior VARX maps the simulated curves into weekly equity returns, the federal funds rate, the Weekly Economic Index, inflation and a bank Marginal Expected Shortfall proxy, with a sign-restricted policy shock adapted to weekly data. Evaluated out of sample from 2017 to 2024, the term-structure block has the lowest forecast error in 13 of 20 maturity and horizon cells, and the density forecasts are well calibrated for the continuously moving variables. At weekly frequency the curve carries no incremental information about these variables once their own lags are controlled for, so the engine's value lies in conditioning on a specified curve path, which no benchmark can do.

title: Calibrating the cosmic distance ladder for independent dark energy constraints
authors: Enya Van den Abeele
abstract: Recent cosmological results presented by the DESI collaboration show a clear deviation from the $Λ$CDM model when considering a time-dependent dark energy equation of state. This deviation is strongly driven by the SNe Ia surveys, which all share the same low redshift sample. The ZTF survey provides the current larger SNe Ia sample at low redshift, which will significantly increase the constraining power. In this context, the LEMAITRE collaboration aims to provide new constraints on dark energy parameters using three independent SNe Ia datasets: ZTF, SNLS and HSC. This effort requires robust photometric calibration, with a particular focus on filter transmission measurement and star catalog calibration. The target for LEMAITRE is to control the calibration systematics on distance moduli below 0.4%.

title: Invertible Transport Between Sample-Only Distributions via Projected Characteristic Functions
authors: Juan Gutiérrez, Victor Gutiérrez-García, José Luis Blanco-Murillo
abstract: Many useful latent distributions can be sampled but do not have a tractable density. Such distributions may be represented by empirical collections of real-world observations or generated by scientific simulators and black-box generative models. These sample-only priors cannot be used directly in likelihood-based normalizing flows, which require evaluating the prior density. We propose Projected Characteristic-Function matching (PCF), a density-free framework for learning an invertible map between a data distribution and a prior specified only through samples. Our method aligns distributions using projected empirical characteristic functions, eliminating the need for density estimation, adversarial training, or paired observations. To address the non-uniqueness of the transport map, we introduce an optional transport regularizer that selects lower-displacement transformations while preserving endpoint alignment. We benchmark PCF on controlled transports, sample-efficiency studies, and high-dimensional alignment tasks. PCF matches the accuracy of kernel MMD on the controlled benchmark and on raw-pixel MNIST--USPS at a cost linear in the batch size, and it is more sample-efficient, achieving lower endpoint error than MMD in 13 of 15 paired runs across library sizes. By avoiding pairwise kernel evaluation, it reduces discrepancy memory by 29.8% and trains at batch sizes where kernel MMD exceeds GPU memory. These results show that PCF provides accurate and efficient invertible transport, particularly in sample- and memory-limited settings.

title: Invariant real curves arising from semiconjugacies of rational maps
authors: Hongxin Sun
abstract: In this paper, we study real analytic invariant curves arising from semiconjugacies of real rational maps. Such semiconjugacies arise naturally in Eremenko's work on invariant Jordan analytic curves. While invariant generalized circles are easy to obtain from real rational maps, we are interested in curves not contained in any generalized circle. First, for a non-exceptional polynomial of degree at least two, we prove that every invariant curve arising from such a semiconjugacy is contained in a generalized circle. Second, in the rational map case, we construct invariant curves arising in this way that are not contained in any generalized circle and have arbitrarily many self-intersections, counted with multiplicity. Moreover, the rational maps can be chosen so that their restrictions to these curves have positive topological entropy.

title: The long-term divergence exponent and the temporal structure of step-to-step perturbations: a simulation study in two passive walking models
authors: Philippe Terrier
abstract: Purpose. Divergence exponents are used to assess the local dynamic stability of gait. Human experiments have related the long-term exponent ($λ_L$) to the complexity of gait fluctuations. Model studies used perturbations without controlled temporal structure. The question was whether $λ_L$ responds to the temporal structure of perturbations in walkers without neuromuscular control. Methods. Two passive walkers, M1 (pilot) and M2 (exploratory), received step-to-step perturbations of five amplitudes ($σ$) and nine temporal structures (ARFIMA parameter $d$), and human stride series of free and metronome walking. Results. At constant amplitude, $λ_L$ increased with $d$ in both models. It was higher with free series than with metronome series or with surrogates. It did not follow $σ$ in M1 and followed $σ$ in M2. Its double dissociation from the short-term exponent was supported in M1 only. In a descriptive analysis, the condition means of $λ_L$ correlated with the scaling exponent of the step durations ($r = 0.980$ in M1 and 0.906 in M2). Conclusion. In two passive walkers with fixed mechanics, $λ_L$ followed the temporal structure of the perturbations; its specificity depended on the model. This response supports the name attractor complexity index (ACI), proposed for $λ_L$ from human experiments.

title: DUV (257 nm) LIDT of Anti-Reflective Coatings
authors: Martin Mydlar, Hana Turcicova, Priyadarshani Narayanasamy, Mihai George Muresan, Ondrej Novak, Jan Vanda, Tomas Tolenis, Jan Brajer, Tomas Mocek
abstract: Laser-induced damage threshold in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) was used to perform tests on AR coated windows intended for industrial processes. The 257 nm wavelength was generated from Yb:YAG fundamental (1030 nm) and the long-term LIDT stability (up to 100000 shots) was selected as representative for minimal industrial qualification. Selected setup for the fourth harmonics generation consists of two stages, generation of second harmonic and subsequently the fourth harmonic with 13,4% conversation efficiency. In both 1-on-1 and S-on-1 experiments, the optics coated with Al2O3/SiO2 by ion beam sputtering technique demonstrated the highest LIDT value of 0.73 and 0.5 J/cm2 respectively. Various damage morphologies, color centers, ballistic damage, delamination, and blistering were observed across the samples with respect to the 1-on-1 and S-on-1.

title: The FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research
authors: Hai Wang, Bretislav Hajek, Chonghe Jiang, Minwei Kong, Ao Qu, Huatian Gong, Bo Dong, Cynthia Barnhart, Jinhua Zhao
abstract: Operations research (OR) relies on algorithms that experts tailor to each problem: a new routing, scheduling or network design problem can take weeks of specialist work before it is solved well at scale. Large language model (LLM) agents now write, test and improve code, but whether they can design algorithms that scale to realistic instances is open: in the FrontierOR benchmark's one-shot evaluation, the strongest model matches Gurobi, with an objective within 1% of Gurobi's and no slower, on only 39% of the large instances. The FrontierOR Challenge asks teams to build agentic workflows that design, test, and improve algorithms for many optimization problems at once. Stage 1 releases 60 of the benchmark's 180 audited problems, spanning six application categories and five formulation types, in weekly rounds of 15; Stage 2 introduces new problems outside the benchmark, with unseen instances. Two tracks are ranked separately: in the Main track we run the submitted algorithms in a network-isolated sandbox with open-source dependencies only; in the Self-hosted track teams solve the instances on their own machines, with any software, within a timed window. Every solution is checked for feasibility, and a feasible solution scores the ratio of its objective to a frozen known reference, averaged over hidden instances.

title: Planning to Stop: Factored Certification and Terminal Repair for Noncircular Robots
authors: Runtian Zheng, Congpeng Zhang, Ying Liu
abstract: Tight-space navigation requires a robot to clear obstacles and stop inside its goal despite uncertainty. We present GeoDiff, a motion-program planner coupling original-goal stopped-set inclusion, witness-guided terminal repair, and factored proof compilation. An exact feasible-translation characterization guides repair; request-local reuse reduces repeated geometric work. We establish conditions for compiler equivalence and reach-and-stop soundness. Across 11,440 floorplan-derived jobs, GeoDiff certifies 61/139 tasks at 5-cm tolerance within 15 s, versus 44/139 for the stop-set baseline. The strongest observed external certificate adapter certifies 13/139 tasks from 119/139 native routes, separating route availability from certification. On tasks derived from public BARN maps, GeoDiff certifies 202/270 at 5-cm tolerance for a Jackal-shaped body, versus 3/270 for the portal baseline. Development analyses distinguish emitter savings from solver coverage, and 1,420 route-tracking episodes characterize the execution interface. These results show how terminal reasoning and proof reuse increase finite-budget certification coverage while preserving the original physical task and goal.

title: MultiBinder: Preventing Multi-Subject Identity Leakage in Personalized Video Generation
authors: Wei Li, Yiheng Zhang, Zhaofan Qiu, Ting Yao, Xiaoyan Sun, Tao Mei
abstract: Personalized video generation faces a significant scalability challenge: as the number of custom subjects increases, existing methods suffer from severe identity leakage and semantic entanglement, resulting in videos with blended attributes and incoherent narratives. We identify that this stems from a lack of explicit binding between textual entity phrases and their corresponding visual patterns prior to fusion in diffusion models. To address this, we propose MultiBinder, a novel framework built on a ``bind-then-narrate'' paradigm. Our approach introduces a two-stage conditioning process before video diffusion. First, Cross-modal Entity Binding devises an entity-aware Q-Former to extract identity-centric features from each subject's reference image and tightly align them with its unique entity phrase, yielding disentangled ``identity tokens.'' Second, a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) acts as a ``narrative director'' in the Narrative-Aware Subject Arrangement stage, capturing the action of each subject from the text prompt and synthesizes contextualized subject features that encapsulate ``who is doing what'' and preserve role-specific distinctions. These features are then injected into a video diffusion model via dedicated conditioning pathways, ensuring precise attribute allocation. Extensive experiments on both general and newly curated multi-subject benchmarks show that MultiBinder significantly outperforms existing methods in multi-subject identity fidelity.

title: One View, One Action: Spatially Generalizable VLAs through Observation-Aligned Experts and Cross Graph Consistency
authors: Jinxi Liu, Ruifeng Zhai, Hao Liu, Guangrun Wang
abstract: Multi-view vision-language-action (VLA) models still face challenges in spatial generalization, particularly under changes in camera viewpoints and robot initial states. These models typically receive action supervision only in the robot base frame, requiring them to implicitly learn the spatial correspondence between observations from each view and base-frame actions. We propose One View, One Action (OVOA-VLA), which learns to predict actions in each view's camera frame, allowing the same physical motion to provide diverse, observation-aligned supervision across views. OVOA-VLA jointly trains a base-frame expert and view-specific action experts, whose robot-state inputs and action targets are expressed in their respective camera frames. Two complementary directed attention graphs model both directions of interaction between the base and view-specific experts, jointly leveraging view-specific action supervision to improve base-frame prediction. Cross Graph Consistency further encourages agreement between the two graphs' base-frame predictions for the same sample. With the same multi-view inputs, the model supports both full and base-only inference. Experiments across multiple simulation benchmarks demonstrate improved manipulation performance and robustness to camera-viewpoint and robot-initialization perturbations. Full and base-only inference achieve average success rates of 88.1% and 85.7% on LIBERO-Plus, respectively. In real-world evaluations, base-only inference raises the average success rates from $π_{0.5}$'s 28.3% to 58.3% across three tasks under spatial distribution shifts.

title: When Foundation Models Disagree: Representational Heterogeneity for Calibrated Uncertainty in Whole-Slide Image Classification
authors: Yekai Shen, Yuqian Wang, Zishun Liao, Rongsheng Wang, Wenting Chen, S. Kevin Zhou, Qingsong Yao
abstract: Pathology foundation models supply strong representations for whole-slide image classification, yet the confidence attached to their predictions remains hard to trust. Prevailing uncertainty estimators act within a single feature space and thereby overlook the uncertainty that the choice of foundation-model representation itself induces. This work introduces CALIFUSE, a calibration-oriented framework that fuses several pathology foundation models for the specific purpose of uncertainty estimation. Departing from accuracy-driven fusion, CALIFUSE reads representational heterogeneity across encoders as an explicit confidence cue. Slide-level decision consensus is coupled with chunk-level evidence agreement quantified through Jensen-Shannon divergence, so that both prediction stability and fine-grained evidence consistency inform the estimate. Foundation-model encoders stay frozen. A task-specific nnMIL classifier is still trained for each FM; CALIFUSE then estimates confidence at inference without training an extra fusion module. Evaluated on seven WSI classification tasks under several foundation-model combinations, the framework sharpens calibration, misclassification detection, and selective prediction relative to both the strongest single-encoder baseline and naive ensemble averaging, all while preserving competitive balanced accuracy.

title: Revisiting Finiteness of Matrix Monoids
authors: Rida Ait El Manssour, Roland Guttenberg, Nathan Lhote, Mahsa Shirmohammadi, James Ben Worrell
abstract: This paper concerns decision problems related to finite monoids of rational matrices. We show that determining finiteness of a given finitely presented monoid is in PSPACE, improving the known $\text{co}{-}\text{NEXP}^{\text{NP}}$ bound. We also show that the membership problem for finite matrix monoids is PSPACE-complete, improving the known NEXP-upper bound. Our two complexity results are corollaries of a new polynomial bit-size bound on matrix entries in finite monoids. This is obtained by reduction to the case of matrix groups, using the structure theory of noncommutative algebras and of matrix monoids. Our techniques also give us a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether a monoid of rational matrices is conjugate to a monoid of integer matrices.

title: Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game
authors: Kevin M. Boergens
abstract: A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. This sweep is optimal against transit in both directions for $q\ge1/2$. At low speeds, $qW_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)/r$ tends to two, and an explicit ten-leg patrol guards width greater than $(2/q-1.235353)r$ throughout $0 < q\le1/40$. Rational spacetime and flux certificates give finite-speed bounds, including $6.944691333740r < W_{\mathrm{opt}}(1/4)\le8.10r$.

title: Log-periodic radiation cores and light rings in pure quadratic bulk gravity
authors: Sudan Hansraj, Rio Bissessur
abstract: In the pure quadratic model of the Böhmer--Jensko bulk--boundary formulation of gravity, every static metric with a regular centre has vanishing central density and pressure, so no affine equation of state admits a regular non-vacuum star. We therefore study singular cores, in scale-invariant variables in which the isotropy condition is a single autonomous relation between two functions. Closures that keep the self-similar solutions as equilibria fix the stability of two vacuum lines but leave that of the matter-bearing equilibria undetermined, except at one unphysical point, so only an equation of state yields definite dynamics. For a linear equation of state the closed system has a focus, a saddle, and a vacuum point with nonzero bulk scalar that exchanges stability with the saddle in a transcritical bifurcation. At the radiation value the system is integrable, through the Tolman integral and scale invariance, and the focus becomes a nonlinear centre surrounded by log-periodic solutions. Radiation is also exactly where the line containing the matter-bearing equilibria of this closure coincides with the line of circular null orbits. Consequently every periodic radiation core with monotonic areal radius has exactly one stable and one unstable light ring per period, at radii forming two interlaced geometric progressions towards the centre with a common ratio tending to 2.165 for small oscillations. In the optical geometry the self-similar solution is a cylinder and each core a periodic tube, whose bulges and necks carry these rings. MIT bag-model configurations whose cores approach these orbits inherit this structure.

title: SCARVA: Interpretable Agentic Reasoning in Software Supply-Chain Analysis
authors: Tim Barsch, Bruno Nogueira, Tobias Wienand, Jan Fopma, Flavio Toffalini
abstract: Complex applications may inherit security vulnerabilities from their dependencies, though a vulnerable dependency does not necessarily endanger the application. Existing tools flag dependencies associated with public vulnerabilities, and more advanced ones analyze the call graph to assess whether the vulnerable code is reachable. However, these approaches are limited to specific programming languages and ecosystems. LLM agents are promising candidates for this task, yet they hallucinate, take shortcuts, and reward hack. As these behaviors are opaque, the agents' conclusions may not be trusted. We present SCARVA a framework designed to produce interpretable reports. SCARVA combines advanced agent reasoning with an evidence-collection methodology that assesses the agent's analysis and improves its trustworthiness. Specifically, the ANALYST performs a software security assessment while SCARVA records every tool call, file access, and web request. Then, one or more independent JUDGE agents inspect the ANALYST's result and produce an evidence-backed report. We evaluate SCARVA on 54 manually curated cases, balanced across exploitable, non-exploitable, and vulnerability-free projects, using both open-weight and frontier models. The best ANALYST model, Qwen 3.8, reaches 82% balanced accuracy and surpasses the evaluated proprietary models. Human annotation validates the JUDGE findings: Claude Opus 5.5 performs best, agreeing with annotators in 94% of claim checks. Finally, we discuss the most common failure modes of agents on supply-chain vulnerability assessment.

title: High-temperature Gibbs states are uniformly Markovian and trivial
authors: Andrew D. Kim, Tai Hsuan Yang, Jong Yeon Lee
abstract: We prove that, above a constant temperature threshold, Gibbs states of local noncommuting qudit Hamiltonians exhibit exponential decay of mutual information and conditional mutual information (CMI). Specifically, we prove exponential decay of the CMI for arbitrary spatial tripartitions $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ which need not comprise the entire system, thereby establishing a \textit{uniform Markov property} for high-temperature Gibbs states. A central obstruction to proving such bounds is that conventional cluster expansions for the logarithm of reduced Gibbs states can fail to converge due to noncommutativity. Our main insight is to construct a classical representation of the Gibbs state using an overcomplete basis. Although such representations generally involve negative quasiprobability weights, we show that a decomposition based on projective 2-designs admits a convergent cluster expansion with strictly positive weights at sufficiently high temperatures, allowing us to circumvent the obstruction. The separability of high-temperature Gibbs states is a natural byproduct of this decomposition. Finally, in the context of mixed-state phases of matter, our results imply that high-temperature Gibbs states belong to the same mixed-state phase as the maximally mixed state.

title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
authors: Omoruyi Atekha, Marcus Greiff, Ray Zhang, Luca Carlone
abstract: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone. Inertial sensing offers a way to observe metric scale, but existing methods add inertial in- formation through a filter or factor graph, which reintro- duces bespoke parameter tuning and optimization costs that can grow with the trajectory. To bridge this gap, we present AnyVIO, a real-time, feed-forward streaming model for monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), which combines a streaming GFM with an inertial foundation model (IFM). Both the GFM and IFM predict the metric motion between consecutive frames, and a lightweight learned fusion head quantifies the reliability of each estimate and blends them in a single forward pass. Across nine datasets recorded from cars, legged and ground robots, and handheld and head- mounted devices, AnyVIO reduces the metric position error of its visual model by 36% while publishing each pose esti- mate 70 ms after an image is received. We further deploy AnyVIO onboard two real vehicles at up to 140 km/h, where it remains accurate in poor lighting and heavy dust.

title: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
authors: Zheyan Wan
abstract: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.

title: Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
authors: Vladimir Juričić, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido
abstract: Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds. Notably, the fractional part of this charge is insensitive to local perturbations of the dislocation core, and it therefore persists after the in-gap core state is removed, as we show analytically in the chain limit and numerically away from it. In the Weyl-semimetal counterpart, the response to a magnetic flux separates this crystalline charge from the charge set by the Chern number of each momentum slice. We propose that a half-integer core charge that persists after the in-gap peak disappears from the local spectrum can be detected in artificial electronic and optical lattices, with metamaterials providing complementary access to the core modes.

title: ScaleWorld: High-Resolution World Generation through Shared Prediction and Refinement
authors: Yansong Qu, Wesker Zheng, Quanjian Song, Zhiyuan Zhang, Xiao Cao, Shengchuan Zhang, Liujuan Cao
abstract: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs. We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone. By refining its own predictions, ScaleWorld produces high-resolution world videos without requiring a separate refinement model. For each video chunk, the shared backbone first completes a low-resolution prediction and then performs one-step high-resolution refinement conditioned on that prediction. To support efficient streaming generation, we maintain separate causal states with a long low-resolution history for prediction and a short high-resolution history for refinement. To address task interference during distillation, we separate specialist optimization from capability consolidation and introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD). This procedure transfers prediction and refinement behaviors from specialized teachers into a shared student through local velocity matching under their respective sampling and history policies. {Extensive experiments demonstrate that ScaleWorld achieves high-quality world generation with improved computational and memory efficiency.

title: Query-Optimal Quantum Minimum Finding from Numerical Estimators
authors: Egil Bae
abstract: We propose a quantum minimum-finding algorithm for objectives accessed via numerical estimators that avoids the logarithmic query overhead of amplifying the confidence of estimates before the search. A coherent estimator that is $\varepsilon$-accurate with probability at least $2/3$ on each of $N$ labels suffices to find a $2\varepsilon$-optimal label using $O(\sqrt N)$ base-estimator queries at constant confidence. The query bound and the additive-error constant are separately worst-case optimal. More generally, suppose a preparation assigns probability mass at least a known $p$ to objective values at most $a$. Without knowing $a$ or the prepared distribution, our algorithm returns a candidate and an estimate $v$ such that, jointly with constant probability, $v$ is $\varepsilon$-accurate for the candidate and $v\le a+\varepsilon$. The algorithm uses $O(p^{-1/2})$ queries to each of the preparation and estimator oracles in the worst case, and the selected candidate can be retained as a quantum state. For preparation width $s_P$ and estimator workspace width $w$, it requires $O(s_P+w+\log\log(4/p))$ qubits, independently of the requested confidence. Applications give worst-case optimal $Θ(\sqrt N/η)$ queries for selecting an $η$-optimal bounded expectation, and guided ground-energy estimation using $O(ω^{-1})$ preparations and $O((ωη)^{-1})$ elementary controlled-evolution queries at constant confidence, where $ω$ is a lower bound on the guiding state's ground-space amplitude overlap.

title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
authors: Amine Lbath, Manan Suri, Aurelien Delaitre, Vadim Okun, Massih-Reza Amini, Dinesh Manocha
abstract: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation. We then measure the consequences of evolving LLM security capabilities in a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data. In 2026 the number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled, with an increasing share rated critical or high, and severe bugs that had survived a decade or more in widely used code were reported several times more often than before. Yet the time between the stages of a vulnerability's life, from report to fix and from disclosure to attack, has not shifted noticeably so far. We grade the mitigations proposed in the literature with an explicit rubric and draw guidance for each group of stakeholders from the best-supported ones.

title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
authors: Calum Murray, Roman Paviot, Martin Kilbinger, Cail Daley, Ken Ganga, Michael J. Hudson
abstract: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able to measure alignment signals by splitting galaxies into colour and morphological samples. We detect tangential alignment of blue disc galaxies at $22.5σ$ and radial alignment of red spheroidal galaxies at $65σ$. By measuring the alignment signal separately around overdensities and underdensities, we show that each of these alignments has the scale and environmental dependence of a linear response to the cosmic tidal field; a response purely quadratic in the Gaussian tidal field, as in classic tidal torque theory is ruled out.

title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
authors: Terence D. Agbeyegbe, Toneukarin G. Agbeyegbe
abstract: Self-consistency certification treats repeated sampling from a language model as sequential evidence accumulation and stops when an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold, guaranteeing finite-sample Type I error control by Ville's inequality. Prior constructions assume sampled rollouts are conditionally independent. We show this assumption fails in practice: reasoning streams are positively correlated through shared reasoning prefixes or across-prompt heterogeneity, changing not merely certificate efficiency but the hypothesis certified. Modeling dependence via a per-unit latent state (the random-effects / intraclass-correlation structure) induces exchangeable, equi-correlated increments with correlation $ρ$. Correlation splits the single null into a realized null about the drawn belief and a population null about average model behavior, which coincide only when $ρ=0$. We show: (i) the standard betting e-process remains anytime-valid for the realized null, not the population null; (ii) read as a population-null test, a suitable mixture has asymptotic crossing probability at least $π=P(μ(Z)>0)$, potentially exceeding nominal $ε$; (iii) the within-unit mean's effective sample size saturates at $1/ρ$, so extra within-unit rollouts cannot restore population validity; and (iv) a prompt-level e-process restores population validity, with optimal allocation at one rollout per prompt under a pure rollout budget. Simulations and Claude Haiku 4.5 rollouts confirm this regime dependence: on GSM8K ($\hatρ=0.435$, $\hatθ=+0.96$) the gap is dormant, whereas on AIME ($\hatρ=0.480$, $\hatθ=-0.15$) the single-unit rule crosses on 24% of prompts at nominal $ε=0.05$, while the prompt-level procedure declines (0.00). This correctness result identifies which reliability claim an anytime-valid certificate actually supports under dependence.

title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
authors: Adrià Ciurana Lanau, Harleen Hanspal, Lusine Abrahamyan, Emilio Tylson Baixauli, Yu Cao, Danai Triantafyllidou, Stefano Zorzi, Gustavo Zanoni Felipe, Peter Griger, Stefan Sietzen, Petru-Daniel Tudosiu
abstract: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers. We present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework built on ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder that encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer. Each candidate conditions a shared decoder to reconstruct its corresponding RGBA layer. For $N$ layers, the representation contains $HW+N$ tokens before backbone-specific packing, compared with $NHW$ for full-grid-per-layer representations. ProtoDiffusion jointly denoises the prototype and a fixed set of candidate slots, conditioned on an image or text, with bounding boxes as optional layout guidance. The model leaves unneeded slots empty and determines the number of layers and, in absence of boxes, their layout, requiring neither as input. The same architecture supports both image-to-design and text-to-design. ProtoVAE achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from its compact shared latent representation, reaching 40.43 dB PSNR on layer crops. On the LayerD evaluation split, image-to-design achieves RGB L1 scores of 0.040 with bounding boxes and 0.057 without, with box-guided alpha soft IoU (0.850) comparable to the strongest fine-tuned baseline (0.871). On merged images, text-to-design reaches 66.41 FID versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein], achieves a 0.860 text-accuracy score, and runs $19.1\times$ faster than the same-backbone generation-then-decomposition cascade.

title: A Success Model at the End of Its Life Cycle: 30 Years of Regionalised Regional Rail in Germany
authors: Lukas Iffländer
abstract: On 1 January 1996, Germany transferred responsibility for regional passenger rail services from the federal government to the states. Three decades later, passenger-kilometres have doubled and competitive tendering has lowered operating costs substantially, making regionalisation the most successful element of the German rail reform. Its organisational model, however, has reached the end of its life cycle: tenders now attract on average only 1.3 bids, 26 contracting authorities and some 60 transport associations maintain overlapping structures, rolling-stock procurement has repeatedly shifted risk onto passengers, and since the Court of Justice of the European Union struck down the German track-access charge cap in 2026, funding no longer covers the ordered service volume. This article reviews the motives and results of regionalisation, identifies three structural design flaws, and argues for a second reform: consolidating authorities, standardising rolling stock, deciding between a repaired market model and integrated public operation, and indexing funding to real infrastructure cost development. The submission contains an English translation followed by the German original.

title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
authors: Rami Atar, Leonid Mytnik, Dominic T. Schickentanz
abstract: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.

title: Optimal Control in Pairs Trading with Negative-Power Utility
authors: Aleksei Kozhevnikov
abstract: We solve a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and utility $U(x)=-x^{-γ}$, $γ>0$. Linearizing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation gives explicit formulas for the value function and the optimal feedback control. A budget inequality and concavity verify optimality over all admissible strategies with nonnegative wealth on every finite horizon, without Novikov's condition. Under the optimal feedback, wealth and consumption admit deterministic upper bounds when the interest rate $r$ is at most the mean-reversion rate $κ$. If $r>κ$, each exceeds any prescribed level with positive probability at every time after the start. If $r>\sqrt{2+γ} κ$, there is an explicit critical horizon at and beyond which expected terminal wealth is infinite, while optimal expected utility is finite. When the critical time falls before maturity, expected wealth at that time is finite exactly when the initial spread is zero. We also show that the suprema of the negative powers of optimal wealth and consumption are integrable on every finite horizon exactly for orders $0<m\le 1+γ$.

title: Topological notions of Shadowing under Semi-Conjugacy
authors: Adarsh Bura, Chris Good
abstract: We study various notions of shadowing and investigate whether they are preserved under semi-conjugacy and inverse limits. In particular, we study Inverse shadowing, $H$-shadowing, Periodic shadowing, Ramsey shadowing, Density shadowing and Ergodic shadowing.

title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
authors: Hao Vo, Taisei Hanyu, Yuki Ikebe, Pham Tri Quang, Sreevenkata Anjani Tishita Godavarthi, Nghi D. Q. Bui, Daniel Sonntag, Chase Rainwater, Duy Minh Ho Nguyen, Anh Nguyen, Ngan Le
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations. All data are generated by a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that combines grasp generation, motion planning, and closed-loop throw optimization under randomized physical properties. We evaluate three representative VLAs, GR00T N1.7, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA, and find that all achieve success rates below 3\%. Our analysis reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success. Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns. We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.

title: Superluminal propagation in the magnetic NED reconstruction of the extremal Dymnikova black hole
authors: J. M. Romero
abstract: We reconstruct the magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) source of the Dymnikova geometry on the branch \(\Iinv>0\) and analyze its electromagnetic perturbations on the fixed background. The reconstruction does not admit a Maxwell limit. The extraordinary characteristic cone gives a transverse speed \(v_\perp^2=(3u-5)/2\), with \(u=r^3/P^3\), which becomes superluminal for \(r>r_{\rm lum}=(7/3)^{1/3}P\). The principal system is pointwise hyperbolic in the finite exterior \(r\ge r_e\), with positive local quadratic energy, but not uniformly hyperbolic up to spatial infinity. The radial effective potential admits an exact reduction, \(V_{\rm em}=f\ell(\ell+1)\mathcal{A}/r^2+ff_{,r}q +f^2(q_{,r}+\frac34q^2)\), behaves as \(V_0\proptoε^2\) near the horizon, and grows as \(27r^4/(4P^6)\) at infinity. It is numerically positive on a fine grid up to \(r=50P\). The Dymnikova reconstruction does not satisfy the hypotheses of the Tomizawa--Suzuki theorem, since it lacks a Maxwell limit, yet it still produces superluminal extraordinary photons. The reconstructed NED branch is therefore mathematically consistent as a source of the Dymnikova background, but not causally acceptable with respect to the physical metric in the asymptotic region. The global positivity of the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum are left as open problems.

title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
authors: Erik Fink, Jingqian Gou, Niklas Holbach, Ondrej Hulik
abstract: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.

title: Minimization of free energy in a Poisson--Boltzmann problem
authors: Shahid Ali, Klemen Bohinc, Angeles Martinez, Stefano Maset
abstract: In this paper, we study a mathematical model in which an ionic solution composed of several types of spherical ions is confined between two uniformly charged parallel planes. The ion concentrations at equilibrium, determined by the interplay between thermal and electrostatic effects, are obtained by minimizing the free energy of the system. The resulting minimization problem is infinite-dimensional, and we prove the existence and uniqueness of its solution by means of a norm-convergence direct method based on the Banach--Saks property of the space in which the problem is posed. The existence proof is technically challenging because the functional to be minimized is not coercive in general. Three illustrative problems are considered and solved numerically.

title: Complete Test Suites for Effectful Automata
authors: Bálint Kocsis, Rick Koenders, Joshua Moerman, Jurriaan Rot
abstract: Complete test suites for automata are (finite) sets of words that enable testing an implementation against a specification: when a (black-box) automaton passes the test suite, completeness guarantees that it is equivalent to the specification on all (infinitely many) words. A well-known method for constructing complete test suites for deterministic automata is the W-method, used in conformance testing and automata learning. Based on a recent categorical generalisation of the W-method, we propose a framework for~the construction and analysis of test suites for a certain class of effectful automata defined by commutative monads. By working in the Eilenberg-Moore category of the associated monad at hand, we obtain a generic notion of effectful W-method, together with a completeness theorem. We show how to apply the framework and derive complete test suites for non-deterministic and weighted automata.

title: Full Kummer Beams: Skyrmionic textures in bichromatic light
authors: Jefferson Delgado-Quesada, Miguel A. Alonso, Eileen Otte
abstract: In this work, we introduce full Kummer beams, the bichromatic analog of full Poincaré beams. To this end, we define three parameters that characterize bichromatic states of polarization and span the Kummer shape, the bichromatic counterpart of the Poincaré sphere. We find that, under certain conditions, full Kummer beams can exhibit skyrmionic textures with a Skyrme number that depends not only on the topological charges but also on the frequencies. These beams can also exhibit emergent behavior upon propagation, including robust, higher-order-like structures and a propagation-invariant Skyrme number over a wide range of beam-waist selections.

title: Exact fermionic decay length and Majorana localization in the sign-alternating kagomé Ising model
authors: Shahane Khachatryan, Hrachya Babujian, Ara SEdrakyan
abstract: We derive an exact fermionic decay length for the sign-alternating kagomé Ising model at fixed transverse momentum $p=π/2$. Writing $x=\tanh K_1$, $y=\tanh K_2$, and $z=\tanh K_3$ for the three dimensionless couplings, the inverse length per lattice cell is $ξ_{\rm f}^{-1}=|\ln(U/|V|)|$, where $U=(1-x^2)(1+y^2z^2)$ and $V=(1+x^2)(y^2-z^2)$. The length diverges at $U=|V|$, with the sign of $V$ selecting one of two classical critical branches. In a simultaneous strong- and weak-bond scaling, these branches become the gap-closing conditions at momenta $0$ and $π$ of the transverse-field Ising chain obtained from the row transfer matrix. On the topological side, the classical decay length tends to the localization length of a Majorana end mode of the Jordan--Wigner fermion chain. We also prove that the regular strong-bond Yang--Baxter family cannot be continued to the finite-coupling interior within the fixed-basis ansatz with one vanishing bond direction.

title: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents
authors: Yicheng Cai, Taegyu Kim, Peng Liu
abstract: Agent applications are increasingly deployed, yet agent-specific attacks pose real threats to them. Upon a security incident, organizations backtrack to identify the CEP (compromise entry point), remediate the damage, and prevent its recurrence. The main artifacts available for backtracking are trajectory logs, which record agent functionalities, and source code; app(lication)-specific function call logs are often fairly limited. However, trajectory logs are at the agent functionality abstraction layer, while the CEP candidates are function calls at the app code execution layer. Due to this semantic gap, the analyst needs to manually inspect the relevant code for each CEP candidate to infer its corresponding agent functionality. In this work, we present Origin, a backtracking tool for the analyst to submit a small number of queries to identify CEPs that existing tools cannot provide. Our approach poses two challenges: (1) define the intermediate abstraction that captures the mapping relationships between the two semantic layers; (2) determine the region-to-variable mapping for constructing the cross-layer graph defined in the intermediate abstraction. Each region is a specific group of agent functionalities. Origin addresses the challenges by (1) the cross-layer dependency graph (CLDG) that connects region-inferred functions at the semantic level to the variables in the low-level taint propagation subgraph, plus the associated query language, and (2) the region inference algorithm. Case studies on five popular agent applications across eight attack incidents show that an analyst using Origin correctly identifies all the CEPs.
